And when that aircraft sits on the ground the tail is only 40 feet above the ground, so he didn't have much clearance. But this guy was a good driver, but what he did was very stupid. When he landed about an hour later his retirement orders were in the hands of the MP officer. That was it. He was finished at midnight that day. That's how fast they act. Because if he would have hit that bridge and that black box would have been laying on the bottom or had it gone off, God knows what would have happened.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What exactly -- When you are talking about the black box, what's the black box?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: That means the nuclear device. That is code for nuclear device. Black box, yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: ______+ information about that. So he had a nuclear device. And so was he on -- When he was launched was he on a mission to bomb?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: Yes. He had interpreted it as a target, and we were going. But in those days, just like now, the target is on the tape. And you put the tape in the pedestal and hit the lever and the tape drives the airplane right to the target.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So he was headed for a target?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: He was headed for that country occupying large wasteland on the other side of the North Pole. You know. There was a phrase that we had in those days, a country occupying large land masses greater than the United States on the other side of the Equator, on the other side of the North Pole, something like that. Very fancy Madison Avenue-type bull shit.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: He was headed there?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: Oh, he was headed, yeah, he and one other guy pulled back. The other guy didn't lose his head. He landed the aircraft safe. A lot of people don't understand. I don't think this is classified. If you have a nuclear device on board, and you send that aircraft off, you bring it back, you land it and park it at the other end of the field, that aircraft is useless for a classified length of time.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Why is that?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: Because the particular characteristics of the nuclear device, that aircraft is useless. You can download it slowly and gingerly, but it stays there. So if you can spook an enemy, he launches 34 percent of his fleet, you have him by the short hairs, because you can call it quits. Hey, we didn't mean it. It is a spook.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So then those planes are useless?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: Useless.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: For how long?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: Indefinitely. That's the word I'll have to use. Indefinite. Yeah, indefinite.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Because it is classified. You can't tell me?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: That's right. I wouldn't dare.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: There are a lot of things that -- it is a business at all costs. A business at all costs. The dollar, the dollar. That's why I never worried about it. At the risk of sounding (inaudible), I have got more than I will ever need, but I never worried about it. I really didn't. And I was looked at as being you are strange. You have got to worry about a dollar, Tom. No, you don't. You worry about your wife and kids and your country and your school and church and synagog. That's what you worry about. Concern yourself about that. In my case I have got to concern myself about some teeth now. I am falling apart. I could walk you across the yard an body parts are falling off. And then the dentists are like garage mechanics or dealers. Mr. Belovich, this is going to cost you $900, to fill up this open space about $1300. Everything is priced.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: And then can you do this?

sp.speaker: Tom Belovich
sp.p: Yes. So he took care of this one. And I'll get around to it. I keep telling my wife, I says Helen, I am 81. I don't want to put a lot of money in my mouth. She says you are going to do it. I said as long as I can strain the olives through it, I'll be all right. [End interview]
